article.headline: Mohammad Zubair Mir: From Political Organisation to Grassroots Engagement in Baramulla
article.dek: A look at his youth mobilisation, political activity and community-facing work across Baramulla.

sections.heading: Education and political beginnings
paragraphs: Mohammad Zubair Mir is associated with the Jammu & Kashmir People’s Conference and has been active in political and community-facing work in Baramulla. His academic background includes Master’s-level study in Money, Banking and Finance at the University of Exeter in the United Kingdom.

His public activity has increasingly centred on youth mobilisation, local political organisation and engagement with neighbourhoods and villages across the district. Local media reported him as District President of the Youth People’s Conference, Baramulla, in December 2025.

sections.heading: Building a youth platform
paragraphs: Youth engagement became a visible part of Mir’s public work during 2025. In August, he held a youth meeting in Old Town Baramulla, bringing young people into a discussion around political participation and local concerns.

In September 2025, the Jammu & Kashmir People’s Conference organised the People’s Cup, a sporting initiative aimed at creating opportunities for young people and encouraging participation beyond formal political spaces.

A further milestone came in December 2025, when the Youth People’s Conference held its first youth convention at D.A.K. Bungalow in Baramulla. The convention marked an effort to give the youth organisation a more visible platform and strengthen its local structure.

sections.heading: Taking political activity into neighbourhoods
paragraphs: During 2026, Mir’s public engagements extended across several parts of Baramulla. A Caravan of Change meeting was held in Old Town in January, followed by meetings and political joining programmes at different locations, including Gulnar Park in Old Town and Jal Sheeri.

Other public interactions included meetings in Qazi Hamam and Kakarhamam in Old Town, as well as outreach in Narwa Block, including Odoora, Namblan, Khal and nearby villages. These engagements reflected an approach focused on direct contact with residents and local political organisation.

sections.heading: Community work and local needs
paragraphs: Community issues have also featured in Mir’s public engagements. In Sangri, a community programme in April 2026 was attended by more than 100 people, according to the account provided for this profile. The engagement was followed by the provision of streetlights in Sangri Ward, which local reporting around 21 April 2026 described as having been arranged through personal funds.

A later public message, titled “Shukriya Sangri”, appeared on 12 May 2026. The sequence of the meeting, the lighting work and the subsequent message became a notable part of his engagement with the area.

Outreach also extended to Dardpora, where an initial visit was followed by a return visit involving streetlights and other items. Lighting assistance was also reported in Gutiyar. These efforts addressed practical concerns raised at the community level.

Close associates have also described Mir as having helped economically weaker sections of society by arranging ration, food and medicines. These accounts form part of the picture of his community-facing work.

sections.heading: Youth, sport and community participation
paragraphs: Sport has been another route for engaging young people. Alongside the People’s Cup, Mir has been associated with activities involving Sultan Warriors and the Chinar Premier League. Sultan Warriors’ victory in the Chinar Premier League final on 15 September 2026 was among the sporting moments highlighted in his public activity.

His support has also extended to volleyball equipment, the Sheeri Blues CF football team and participation as a special guest at the Balkote Uri Volleyball Smash Bash 2026. Such events offer a way to connect with young people through local teams and community sport.

sections.heading: Engagement with traders and civic concerns
paragraphs: Mir has also met representatives of the local trading community, including a meeting with the GMC Kantbagh Trader Federation in July 2026. Public commentary associated with his activities has addressed issues such as employment and recruitment, roads and infrastructure, food safety and the local economy.
Across these engagements, the recurring themes have been youth opportunity, neighbourhood-level needs and the expectation that public representatives remain accessible and accountable.

sections.heading: A continuing grassroots presence
paragraphs: The record of meetings, youth programmes, political joining events, sports activities and community interventions shows a public profile developing through repeated contact with people in different parts of Baramulla. The significance of that work will ultimately be measured by its continuity, the response of residents and the practical outcomes it delivers.

For now, Mohammad Zubair Mir’s public activity reflects an effort to combine political organisation with local engagement—bringing youth, traders and neighbourhood concerns into the centre of his work.
